input.quote: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 2.1 binds us (Customer) to a multi-year USD 2,000,000 per year take-or-pay commitment expressly "without reduction or termination rights." That is the rule's walk-away position: it fails the fallback, which allows a commitment only for the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised. It also contradicts § 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no minimum-volume commitment, and § 7.1, which limits us to Fees stated in Order Forms. The redline restores the preferred position (pay only for Services ordered or used) while carrying the fallback parameters for any Order Form volume commitment.

ops.oldText: 2.1 Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
ops.newText: 2.1 Customer has no minimum purchase or take-or-pay commitment. Customer pays only for Services it actually orders or uses under an Order Form. Any volume commitment must be set out in an Order Form, may not exceed the then-current twelve-month term, may be reduced by Customer on thirty days' written notice, and any shortfall is settled by a true-up of the unpurchased amount rather than a penalty.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a three-year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination right, so we have replaced it with payment for Services actually ordered or used, consistent with § 12.3's confirmation that we make no minimum-volume commitment. If a commitment is commercially necessary, we can work within a single 12-month term that is reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up instead of a penalty.
proposal.summary: Remove the three-year take-or-pay minimum; fees for ordered or used Services only, with a capped, reducible commitment and true-up as fallback.
